scope: Original promo versus supplied original desktop/mobile closed/open visual evidence only

reviews.inspection_method: Each of the five original images independently loaded through vision_analyze; no boards substituted.
reviews.reason: Desert silhouette, shallow relief, outcrop cluster and hardware are consistent between promotional and runtime images; visible limitations are aesthetic rather than established geometry defects.
reviews.hardware: Brass front strap, round lower fitting, side ring, lid-corner caps and dark rock-like feet persist. Open rear fittings and released strap are visible; no definite detachment established.
reviews.terrain: Low tan dune relief and dark angular rear outcrop read in both closed views. The clustered outcrops merge visually into a single mass; individual count cannot be certified from these angles.
reviews.texture: Promo has richer fine mineral/rock detail and grounding shadows; runtime is softer and brighter. Both body treatments can read as pale wood rather than mineral sand.
reviews.mobile: Complete closed/open model fits without apparent clipping. Shallow dunes and small brass details are less readable than the box silhouette; supporting UI copy is small.
reviews.open: Hollow cavity, plain warm lid underside and dark rim visible on both sizes. Lid-top dunes/outcrops are out of sight as expected.
concerns: Conspicuous dark closed seam makes lid appear slightly raised, also present in promo and disclosed in README; not a proven closure defect.
Dune/material specificity remains modest; no photorealistic desert claim supported.
limitations: Static original-image inspection only; runtime checks were reported passing by the task context and were not rerun here.
No rear-open view, continuous animation, physical-phone test, manufacturing certification, or hidden-surface inspection in this review.
Hidden rear hinges and the released open-state latch are not independently evidence of failure. Lid-top ornament is naturally occluded in front-open views.
Promotional lighting and microtexture are not proof of corresponding modeled detail. This is a bounded visual review, not final approval.

Dark closed seam is visually strong but does not establish faulty seating.
Promotional finish should not be described as literal runtime ceramic gloss.

reviews.inspection_method: Each of the five original images independently loaded through vision_analyze; no boards substituted.
reviews.reason: No proven geometry failure, but the promo makes the crater cavity distinctly more readable than default runtime views; decide whether that fidelity/legibility gap is acceptable.
reviews.hardware: Gold front clasp and corner protectors with dark block feet present consistently. No need to invent side rings or lower round hardware absent from this design. Rear open fittings are small but not visibly broken.
reviews.terrain: Promo shows clear recessed gray crater within a green volcanic mound, five pale-edged green cays and a thin pale reef arc. Runtime retains mound, five cays and arc, but summit reads more like a notch/uneven peak than an obvious cavity.
reviews.texture: Promo charcoal surface and finely textured terrain are richer than runtime blue-gray mottled stone and faceted green slopes. This is chiefly surface/lighting simplification; no missing map or torn geometry evident.
reviews.mobile: Volcano/cays and complete closed/open model remain framed. Crater cavity is particularly hard to read; long title uses three lines and pushes lower page content down, not model clipping.
reviews.open: Hollow dark cavity, green-gray rim and plain raised inner lid visible. Terrain is occluded on far side; released latch is expected.
concerns: Crater prominence is stronger in promo than runtime at supplied camera/scale. README acknowledges summit legibility limitations and reports measured crater depth; this review does not contradict that geometry evidence.
Thin reef reads as decorative wire rather than living reef.
reviews.decision_required: Art-direction decision only: accept disclosed crater legibility gap between promo and default desktop/mobile view, or request a separate camera/presentation refinement. No art changed and no geometry-failure claim.

reviews.inspection_method: Each of the five original images independently loaded through vision_analyze; no boards substituted.
reviews.reason: Tree/body geometry and framing are coherent, but promo promises a materially darker, more textured green lid and more detailed foliage/forest floor than the pale simplified runtime appearance.
reviews.hardware: Front clasp, lower round fitting, side ring, corner caps and gray irregular feet retained; open hinges and released strap visible without clear unintended intersections.
reviews.terrain: Three rooted trees with tallest central crown and elongated green ground island remain readable in both closed sizes. Promo crowns have fine leaf-like marks and textured ground; runtime uses smooth flattened lobes and simpler terrain. No missing tree or detached root demonstrated.
reviews.texture: Promo lid reads dark forest-green and finely pebbled, with moss-like floor and fine bark/leaf texture. Runtime lid top is pale sage, canopy smoother, and body strongly scored wood/earth. README discloses lighting-induced pale lid and stylized canopy, but this is the strongest finish mismatch in this set.
reviews.mobile: All three trees and rooted bases readable; full closed/open model fits. Small hardware and interior detail are reduced but no apparent cropping.
reviews.open: Green plain underside, rim and empty bark-toned cavity visible. Trees naturally hidden behind lid; absence is not an attachment failure.
concerns: Promotional microtexture and dark green material impression should not be represented as an exact runtime match.
Scored wood character and blunt miniature roots remain stylized limitations, not demonstrated structural faults.
reviews.decision_required: Decide whether the disclosed pale/smooth runtime finish is acceptable alongside the richer dark-green promo, or request separate presentation/material reconciliation. No final approval or edits.
